Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Capture the last thing you played, even when not recording

If you played something great without recording, press ⇧R (Flashback Capture) and Logic turns it into a region. MIDI can be captured whether the project is playing or stopped. Audio capture arrived in Logic 11.2: give the audio track focus and play the project. Logic saves audio only while there is an incoming signal, needs at least four seconds of playback, and keeps up to one minute.

⇧R

Source Apple — Capture a recent audio performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Capture your most recent MIDI performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — What's new in Logic Pro for Mac 11.2 · Logic Studio Training — Logic Pro 11.2 Update: Flashback Recording

Section 09 · Marquee Tool Tricks

Make Marquee your ⌘-click tool

Make Marquee your Command-click tool. In the Tracks area, click the Command-click Tool menu and choose the Marquee tool. From then on, hold ⌘ and drag to marquee-select parts of regions on one or more tracks. Release ⌘ and you're back on your Left-click tool. The Command-click Tool menu only appears when Enable Complete Features is on, in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced.

⌘ + drag

Source Apple — Overview of tools in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Sound On Sound — Marque Of Distinction · Apple — Assign tools in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Use the complete set of features in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Split any mixed audio into stems

Control-click an audio region and choose Processing > Stem Splitter. Since 11.2 it separates up to six stems — vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and other — and it needs an Apple silicon Mac.

Source Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac · Why Logic Pro Rules — Logic Pro 11.2 Update is Out! Improved Stem Splitter · Production Expert — Apple Updates Logic Pro with Improved Stem Separation

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Give every row a different step rate

Rows do not have to share the pattern's step rate. Click a row header to select the row, then in the Step Sequencer inspector click Row and choose a note value from the Step Rate pop-up menu. To change just one step, switch to Step Rate edit mode and drag vertically in that step. Hats at 1/16 and kick at 1/8 each run at their own speed.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit Step Sequencer rows in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Change the musical length of a pattern in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Chord ID reads chords off audio, not just MIDI

Drag a guitar demo, a piano take or a rough bounce onto the Chord track. Chord ID analyses the region and adds the chords it finds to the Chord track as a chord group. It works on audio and MIDI regions, and Apple says it handles single instruments and full mixes.

Source Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

Section 12 · Logic Drummer Tricks

Convert a Drummer region to MIDI and edit it by hand

Right‑click the region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. You get the full performance in the Piano Roll to nudge, delete and re‑velocity as you like.

Source Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

Questions

Before you buy.

Which version of Logic does it cover?

It works with Logic Pro 11 and 12. Every key command is the factory default on a US keyboard, and where a command could move between versions the book gives the command name and menu path instead. Section 18 covers the Logic Pro 11 features: Session Players, the Chord track, Stem Splitter, ChromaGlow. Section 19 covers Logic Pro 12: the Synth Player, Chord ID, and the fact that 12 runs only on Apple silicon.

I have never used Logic. Is it for me?

Yes. Start Here walks you through your first session in 10 steps, 40 tricks are marked safe for your first day, and every Logic word the book uses is explained in plain English in a 48-word glossary.

How do I know the tricks are right?

Every trick shows the source it was checked against, usually Apple's own Logic Pro guide, with a live link. Anything that could not be confirmed against a source was cut rather than printed on a guess.

Is this a video course?

No. It is 249 written tricks: title, what it does, the key command. Most take ten seconds to read.

Do I need any third-party plugins?

No. Every trick uses stock Logic Pro. Nothing to buy, nothing to install.

What exactly do I get?

Two files. The PDF: 89 pages, clickable contents and bookmarks in the sidebar. The searchable library: one file you open in any browser, where you type what you want to do (record vocals, make a beat) and the right tricks come up first. Both are yours to keep and both work offline.

How is it delivered?

Instantly, through Gumroad, the same store as my plug-ins. You get a download link on screen and by email as soon as the payment clears.
